narrative: OMX30 enters Friday in a technically overbought state with RSI 77.4 and Stochastic 93.4, both deep into mean reversion territory despite maintaining a bull regime (+6.0% vs 200-MA, strong ADX 66.0). However, the negative correlation signal (-0.203%), S&P 500 weakness (-0.35%), and NASDAQ selloff (-0.39%) create a downstream headwind that cannot be ignored. US 10Y yields surged +210bps to 5.103%, pressuring Swedish growth and tech valuations while benefiting banks. USD/SEK strength (+0.83%) is a modest positive for industrials exporters, but the Nvidia scandal narrative is creating sector-wide sentiment damage in technology. At 52W highs with limited upside room, the risk-reward tilts cautiously defensive.
morningBrief: OMX30 faces a mixed Friday setup: technically overbought (RSI 77, Stoch 93) but entrenched in a strong bull trend (+6% vs 200-MA, ADX 66). Key tension: negative overnight correlation (-0.203%) and weak US equities (-0.35% S&P) suggest choppy consolidation above 3123 support rather than extension. Watch 3180 (50-MA resistance) and 3085 (lower Bollinger band) for bounce-back mechanics. Banks catch a bid from US 10Y yield surge (5.103%), but tech/growth gets pinned by DCF compression and NASDAQ weakness. USD/SEK at 10.05 supports Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson exports but sentiment fragile. Industrials likely outperform defensive rotation; H&M pressured by weak EUR/SEK. No major Swedish data today; US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET will be watched for Fed trajectory clues. Recommendation: trade tight ranges, avoid chasing highs, wait for clearer directional setup.
